title: Asynchronous prefetch & hybrid TP/PP scaling scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory notes on an experiment series to characterize how asynchronous KV/prefix prefetch + host staging interacts with combined tensor-parallel (TP) and pipeline-parallel (PP) placements. Goal is to identify common jitter/bandwidth cliffs that harm tail latency when we try to push throughput with hybrid parallelism and to generate small, actionable mitigations.

Background/context:
- Running medium-large models in hybrid config (TP 4 x PP 2) to raise throughput while staying within per-GPU memory.
- We introduced an async prefetch mechanism for KV cache + weight prefetch into host pinned buffers to overlap PCIe transfers with compute.
- Observed intermittent 99.9th increases when bursts of long sequences and many warm cache-misses coincide. Hypothesis: host staging, PCIe bursts and driver scheduling interact with NCCL collectives and cause pauses that amplify in multi-stage PP handoffs.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Variables: placement topology (intra-node NVLink ring vs cross-node NVLink/PCIe), prefetch mode (sync, async immediate, async delayed), host-staging buffer size (64MB, 256MB, 1GB), NVSwitch partitioning (all-to-all vs islanded), NCCL algorithm hint (ring/tree), CPU pinning for prefetch threads (none, core-affine).
- Workloads: synthetic prompt mix: 50% short (16 tokens), 30% medium (256 tokens), 20% long (2048 tokens) to trigger KV cache dynamics.
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency, token throughput, PCIe bandwidth (nvlink-smi + perf counters), host-to-device post-copy times, NCCL collective stall counters, dmesg gpu errors, scheduling preemption logs.

Quick setup notes and commands used:
- Tensor/PP layout: TP=4 (tensor split across 4 GPUs), PP=2 (stages across two host cards).
- Prefetch daemon launched with taskset -c 4-7 to isolate CPU cores.
- Traces: used perf + nvprof + custom RPC tracing. Example commands:
  - nsys profile --output=run1 --trace=nvtx,cuda,nvtx --duration=120s 
  - sudo perf record -e cycles:u -a -g -- sleep 120
  - nvidia-smi dmon -s u -o DT --loop-ms=100 > sdbw.csv &

Observations (raw):
- When prefetch threads were not core-affined, we saw 2x variance in prefetch latency (host staging times). Pinning threads to CPU cores adjacent to GPU PCIe root complex reduced variance by ~40%.
- Large host-staging buffers (1GB) reduced average number of small DMA ops but created periodic long PCIe bursts (~200ms) that lined up with PP boundary handoffs and caused 99.9 spikes.
- Smaller buffers (64MB) produced more frequent but shorter DMA ops; tail latency improved modestly (p99.9 down ~12%) at cost of 6% higher CPU utilization.
- Cross-node hybrid layouts where PP stage boundary crossed the node boundary showed worst tails: NCCL collectives were delayed due to sudden extra host-to-host RDMA + unexpected PCIe queue storms on the sender side.
- NCCL algorithm hint 'tree' reduced max stall time in some cross-node configs compared to 'ring', likely because tree spreads traffic and avoids momentary bisection congestion.
- Enabling prefetch batching (coalesce multiple small prefetches into one transfer when queued within 10ms) smoothed PCIe bandwidth and reduced p99/p99.9. But batching too aggressively increased cold-start per-request latency for first tokens.

Mini case: trace snippet (simplified timeline)
- 0ms: request arrives to PP-stage0 (GPU0), triggers KV miss and issues async prefetch for keys for tokens 1..n
- 3ms: prefetch daemon queues 8 small transfers into host staging buffer
- 10ms: compute on TP shards running; transfers not yet flushed
- 42ms: host staging flush starts -> PCIe burst 120ms (due to 1GB chunk)
- 160ms: PCIe burst completes but PP-stage1 waiting on kv links; NCCL allreduce attempt times out partial -> fallback collective -> extra 80ms -> p99.9 spike

Profiling artifacts / signals to look for:
- CPU: high softirq and PCIe DMA scheduling spikes around tail events
- GPU: sudden drop in SM utilization while transfers saturate link counters
- NCCL: rise in 'op stalls' counter and extra retries in logs
- Kernel: 'nvidia 0000:xx:xx: DMA engine' messages and occasional driver warning about resource starvation

Actionable mitigations tested (and quick results):
1) CPU pin prefetch threads to dedicated cores near NIC/GPU -> reduces variance. (adopt as default for async daemon)
2) Adaptive prefetch sizing: cap host staging flush to 128MB per flush and apply small multi-transfer coalescing window (10ms) -> balanced tail improvement (~15% p99.9 reduction) with small extra CPU usage.
3) Topology-aware PP placement: avoid splitting PP boundary across node when possible; prefer intra-node handoff (even if slightly less memory-balanced) -> biggest single win for tails in our cluster config.
4) NCCL hints per topology: prefer tree for cross-node PP boundaries; keep ring for intra-node NVLink fully-connected clusters. Add logic into placement heuristics.
5) Backpressure on prefetch queue: if NCCL or PCIe bandwidth saturating, temporarily pause coalescing to avoid creating large bursts. Proof-of-concept helped remove the worst spikes.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Interaction with GPU GPU-direct RDMA: do RDMA-enabled NICs reduce host-staging bursts in cross-node PP handoffs? Need a node-level test with Mellanox GPUDirect enabled.
- If we introduce per-request priority, can we preempt prefetch flushes to let small synchronous transfers through during PP handoffs? Complexity vs benefit TBD.
- Explore scheduler-level pacing: throttle application-level DMA submission rate based on link utilization counters exposed by driver. Prototype cost/benefit.
- Test with real customer workload (dialog mix with many short turns) to validate findings under production traffic.

Notes to self / todo:
- Re-run key config with per-core counters and collect perf maps (2025-03-05 planned).
- Pull full nsys traces for the 3 worst runs and upload to MR for review.
- Add a tiny feature flag to prefetch daemon to toggle coalescing window and buffer cap; run A/B on Dedicated cluster.

Summary (one-paragraph):
Asynchronous prefetch + host staging can meaningfully improve average throughput in hybrid TP/PP setups, but naive large-buffer flushes create PCIe bursts that interact poorly with PP handoffs and NCCL collectives, producing tail latency cliffs. The most robust mitigations so far are topology-aware placement (avoid cross-node PP boundaries when possible), pinned prefetch threads, and a conservative flush policy that balances burst size and coalescing window. Further tests with RDMA and preemptible prefetch flushes may yield additional wins.

- [Rafael] Run RDMA-enabled node tests and report (due 2025-03-12)
- [Maya] Prepare A/B test plan for Dedicated cluster and alerting thresholds for p99.9 (due 2025-03-10)

End of scratchpad.
